```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
source("meta_analysis.R", local = TRUE)
source("utils.R", local = TRUE)
run <- params$run
results <- run$metaRes
estimated <- results[is.finite(results$r), , drop = FALSE]
used <- run$used_data
filters <- function(x) if (length(x)) paste(x, collapse = ", ") else "All"
```

# Selection and method

Analysis run: **`r run$created`**.

- Outcome: **`r run$outcome_label`**.
- Age groups: `r filters(run$selection$ages)`.
- Publication years: `r filters(run$selection$years)`.

This report uses the data, filters, labels and fitted models saved together when the analysis was run. Changing the app filters requires a new analysis before exporting a report.

For each of the five BESSI domains, correlations are transformed to Fisher's *z*. The existing random-effects model is fitted with REML using `metafor::rma.mv`, with matrix identifiers nested within paper identifiers (`random = ~ 1 | paper_id / matrix_id`) and t-based inference. Pooled correlations and confidence limits are back-transformed to *r*. Standard errors and heterogeneity variances remain on the Fisher *z* scale.

The model represents clustering within papers. It does not fully account for every form of participant overlap or correlated sampling error, including overlaps across different papers. The database is intended for exploratory synthesis; study-specific notes remain relevant when interpreting a result.

# Data coverage

The estimated models use **`r length(unique(used$paper_id))` articles**, **`r length(unique(used$matrix_id))` matrices**, and **`r nrow(used)` observed skill–outcome correlations**. Counts below are specific to each skill, so the same matrix can contribute to several domains.

Ns are the reference sample sizes already coded in the database. The sum of those Ns is **not a count of unique people**: sample overlap may be present, and the available N may differ between correlations. Ns have not been automatically replaced with pair-specific values.

```{r coverage, results='asis'}
report_table(meta_coverage_table(run$data, results$skill, run$labels),
  caption = "Available usable data by skill before model fitting")
```

Missing correlations do not contribute to a model. “Invalid values” counts observed correlations that cannot be analyzed because r is non-finite or outside −1 < r < 1, or the reference N is non-finite or at most 3. It does not count ordinary missing correlations. The downloadable data identify the reason; source values are retained. Skills with fewer than two usable matrices, or a model error, are marked as not estimable.

```{r descriptives, results='asis'}
report_table(meta_sample_table(used), caption = "Matrices contributing to estimated models")
```

# Results

```{r results, results='asis'}
report_table(meta_results_table(results, run$labels), caption = "Meta-analysis results")
```

```{r model-details, results='asis'}
cat('<details><summary>Model details</summary>\n')
cat('<p>SE and heterogeneity variance (tau-squared) are on the Fisher z scale. Q is the heterogeneity test statistic.</p>\n')
report_table(meta_results_table(results, run$labels, details = TRUE),
  caption = 'Technical model details')
cat('\n</details>\n')
```

```{r model-notes, results='asis'}
for (i in which(nzchar(results$note))) {
  cat("\n\n**", run$labels[results$skill[i]], ":** ", results$note[i], "\n", sep = "")
}
if (nrow(estimated)) {
  largest <- which.max(abs(estimated$r))
  cat("\n\nThe largest absolute pooled association among the estimated domains is for **",
    run$labels[estimated$skill[largest]], "** (*r* = ",
    formatC(estimated$r[largest], digits = 3, format = "f"), ").\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("\n\nNo model could be estimated.\n")
}
```

The figure below shows estimates and 95% confidence intervals on the correlation (*r*) scale, for domains with an estimated model.

```{r pooled-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
if (nrow(estimated)) print(meta_result_plot(results, run$labels, run$outcome_label))
```

# Forest plots

Forest plots identify each contributing matrix by authors, year and matrix code. Tick labels and estimates are displayed as correlations (*r*), with positions along a Fisher *z* axis. Only successfully estimated domains are plotted.

```{r forest-plots, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
for (skill in names(run$outList)) {
  model <- run$outList[[skill]]
  if (!is.null(model)) meta_forest_plot(model, run$labels[skill])
}
```
